1.w: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes in the Diaspora: Greetings.

2.w: Esteem [it] all joy, my brothers, when you⁺ might fall into various trials,

3.w: knowing that the testing of your⁺ faith produces perseverance.

4.w: And let endurance have [its] perfect work, so that you⁺ may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

5.w: Now if any of you⁺ lacks wisdom, let him ask from God, the One giving generously to all and not reproaching, and it will be given to him.

6.w: But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one doubting is like a wave of the sea, being blown and being tossed by the wind.

7.w: For let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord.

8.w: [He is] a double-souled man, unstable in all his ways.

9.w: But let the brother of humbleness boast in his exaltation,

10.w: and the one who [is] rich in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of grass.

11.w: For the sun rose with [its] burning heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. Thus also the rich [man] will fade away in his pursuits.

12.w: Blessed [is] the man who endures trial, because, having been approved, he will receive the crown of life that He promised to those loving Him.

13.w: Let no one being tempted say, “I am being tempted from God.” For God is unable to be tempted by evils, and He Himself tempts no one.

14.w: But each one is tempted, being dragged away and being enticed by [his] own desire.

15.w: Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, having become fully grown, brings forth death.

16.w: Do not be misled, my beloved brothers.

17.w: Every good act of giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.

18.w: Having willed [it], He brought us forth by the word of truth, for us to be a certain firstfruits of His creatures.

19.w: Know [this], my beloved brothers: But let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger;

20.w: for man’s anger does not produce the righteousness of God.

21.w: Therefore, having put off all filthiness and abundance of wickedness, accept in meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your⁺ souls.

22.w: But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deluding yourselves,

23.w: because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, this one is like a man observing his natural face in a mirror,

24.w: for he observed himself and has gone away, and immediately he forgot what kind he was.

25.w: But the one having looked intently into the perfect law, that of freedom, and having continued in [it], not having been a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work—this one will be blessed in his doing.

26.w: If anyone thinks to be religious, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, the religion of this one [is] futile.

27.w: Pure and undefiled religion before the God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their tribulation, to keep oneself unstained from the world.
